entityDescription:
ANcybernetics is an Italian deep-tech company developing bio-inspired autonomous underwater robotic systems for environmental monitoring, infrastructure inspection and the collection of high-quality subsea data. Founded as an academic spin-off of Università Politecnica delle Marche (UNIVPM), ANcybernetics has been registered in the Italian Special Register of Innovative Start-ups since September 2024.
The company designs and develops compact Biomimetic Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (BAUVs) combining bio-inspired propulsion, autonomous navigation, modular sensor integration and onboard artificial intelligence. Its flagship platform, POSEIDRONE, uses fin-based propulsion inspired by fish locomotion instead of conventional propellers, enabling high manoeuvrability while reducing disturbance to the surrounding environment and seabed.
POSEIDRONE is designed to perform autonomous and repeatable missions and can be deployed directly from shore or from small vessels, reducing the logistical complexity typically associated with underwater robotic operations. Its modular architecture allows the platform to be configured according to the specific mission and data requirements, integrating optical cameras, acoustic sensors, environmental probes and other specialised payloads. Onboard computing and AI enable real-time data processing, perception and the identification of features or anomalies of interest.
ANcybernetics targets applications including the inspection and monitoring of submerged infrastructure, ports, pipelines, cables, reservoirs and coastal assets, as well as seabed mapping, marine habitat monitoring, biodiversity assessment and environmental data collection. The company is developing solutions aimed at making underwater monitoring more autonomous, scalable, repeatable and accessible, while reducing human exposure to hazardous underwater operations.
ANcybernetics develops its core robotic, control and autonomy technologies in-house and is building an ecosystem of specialised sensors, communication systems and industrial partners around its platforms. The company is also exploring the integration of underwater robotics with satellite-enabled services, including satellite navigation, Earth Observation and satellite communications, to support georeferenced surveys, remote operations and integrated monitoring of maritime, coastal and water-related assets.
Through its combination of robotics, AI, bio-inspired engineering and environmental sensing, ANcybernetics aims to bridge the gap between traditional remotely operated vehicles and large, complex autonomous underwater systems, enabling a new generation of flexible and cost-effective subsea monitoring services.

entityDescription:
Martinr B.V. is a Netherlands-based micro-enterprise specialising in front-end development and user interface design for space engineering, Earth observation, human spaceflight and civil protection.
Core capabilities: front-end web application development in TypeScript, user experience design for complex technical and scientific data, interactive data visualisation and dashboards, design systems and accessibility, and real-time and interactive web applications. Technologies include TypeScript, React, WebRTC, WebGL and mapping libraries, and REST/OpenAPI integration.
The company draws on four years of experience delivering software for ESA and related institutional programmes within teams at Starion Group, ATG Europe and Space Applications Services. This work included review interfaces for ECSS-E-TM-10-25 models in support of model-based systems engineering (UI-DSM), an ESA Earth Observation mission database supporting capability mapping and long-term planning (EORSA-DB), a live meeting tool used during Axiom Mission 4 to connect the ISS crew with audiences on Earth, and the PPRD Med disaster prevention and response platform. This provides working familiarity with ECSS standards, MBSE tooling and ESA review processes.
Martinr B.V. is available to ESA and to prime contractors as a subcontractor or consortium partner for front-end development, UI/UX design, data visualisation and interactive web applications.

Impact Ninja is a specialised Poland-based consultancy and expert firm focused on social impact evaluation, evidence-based assessment, and narrative modeling for research, technology, and innovation.Founded and led by Dr. Marta Wróblewska—a leading European expert on impact assessment with a PhD from the University of Warwick—the firm integrates academic rigor with practical policy experience. Dr. Wróblewska brings extensive experience from the public agency sector, having served in operational and strategic roles at the National Centre for Research and Development (NCBR) in Poland, where she also chaired expert evaluation panels. Her research has been supported by major competitive research grants (including the Volkswagen Stiftung and NCN) and active membership in the Research on Research Institute (RoRI) at University College London (UCL). She is author of a PhD Thesis, a practical ebooks and several academic papers dedicated to research impact evaluation policies and related institutional change.

Impact Ninja offers a complete suite of impact assessment services, including strategic verification, custom narrative modeling, and executive training. The firm’s methodologies are continuously informed by state-of-the-art international research. Having advised dozens of institutions across diverse disciplines and trained hundreds of experts, Impact Ninja specializes in translating complex scientific, technological, and corporate efforts into clear, credible, and measurable social outcomes.

Key Competencies for ESA & Corporate Evaluation:Methodological Rigor: Application of evidence-backed narrative and analytical models developed through extensive research into institutional impact.Agency & Public-Sector Experience: Deep familiarity with institutional review processes, panel management, and multi-stakeholder governance.International Expertise: Direct involvement in shaping European research evaluation standards via international research networks (UCL RoRI, VW Stiftung).Impact Optimization & Communication: End-to-end support in articulating, auditing, and refining the societal value generated by large-scale R&D and innovation programs.

entityDescription: Klimaforge AS is a Norwegian company building satellite-based evidence infrastructure for EU forest regulation and forest-carbon markets. Its EUDR compliance engine turns Copernicus Sentinel-1/2 change detection into audit-ready compliance verdicts by cross-checking flagged forest clearings against independent government land registries — live today in Norway and Germany — rather than relying on supplier-submitted paperwork. A parallel above-ground biomass platform, using satellite radar, optical and spaceborne LiDAR data, extends the same detection core into forest-carbon measurement, reporting and verification (MRV), delivered nationally in Estonia and piloted in Norway. Klimaforge is downstream of ESA's Earth Observation systems (Copernicus Sentinel-1/2, NASA GEDI, ALOS PALSAR-2) and is preparing to launch commercially in Norway from January 2027.

Entity Description / Overview:
SustainGenix GmbH (Lörrach, Germany) is a space-downstream software, social impact, and geo-information enterprise specialising in high-altitude climate resilience, spatial risk analytics, and off-grid hazard intelligence. The company owns and governs the intellectual property of the 1,700 km Great Himalaya Trail (GHT) spatial dataset, built upon fifteen years of georeferenced field exploration, high-altitude mapping, and extensive research on tourism impacts across fragile mountain ecosystems.
SustainGenix develops the "Human-Digital Twin" Safety Engine, a 3-tier technology architecture bridging space-borne sensors with community-based observation and research, and storytelling:

Space Layer: Ingestion and automated processing of European Space Agency (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) data for cloud-penetrating interferometry (InSAR), surface deformation tracking, and Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) monitoring across complex mountain terrain.

AI & Cloud Layer: Dialect-adapting, offline-first speech-to-text AI models (Sherpa, Tamang, Nepali) and serverless cloud analytics that convert spoken local reports into structured, georeferenced spatial vectors and real-time B2B enterprise risk APIs.

Ground-Truth & Community Layer: Deployment of ruggedised satellite communicators and mobile tools to local micro-entrepreneurs (female teahouse hosts) and licensed trekking guides. This layer functions both as an off-grid safety network and as a digital platform for community storytelling, preserving cultural heritage and publishing local narratives in native dialects.

Research & Commercial Capabilities: SustainGenix conducts field research into mountain tourism impacts, socio-economic equity, and climate adaptation. The company actively promotes responsible tourism along Himalayan corridors by supporting firewood elimination, waste management, and direct economic inclusion. SustainGenix commercialises its spatial assets through enterprise hazard APIs for tour operators and travel insurers (Duty of Care compliance), B2C dynamic safety navigation apps (FarOut, OutdoorActive and ride with GPS, B2G/NGO cryosphere change analytics, and white-label "Dynamic Trail OS" software licensing for international mountain trail authorities worldwide.

description:
NEMA Systems Ltd combines advanced electrical and electro-mechanical design capability, decades of aerospace, defence and space actuation and certification experience and established UK manufacturing capability to develop and industrialise high-performance motors, power electronics, drives and actuation systems. Our integrated approach brings together engineering, manufacturing and test capability to reduce development risk, accelerate programmes and provide customers with a single, experienced partner for demanding applications.
Quality and traceability are embedded throughout our approach. Decades of experience through our parent company NEMA Ltd allows us to design and manufacture to AS9100 Rev D, alongside ISO 9001 and relevant OEM supplier approvals. Space-product development and assurance activities are aligned with the requirements of ISO 14300-1:2023 and ISO 14300-2:2023, together with the applicable ISO/ECSS technical standards identified through the project requirements and compliance matrix. Specific actuator verification and qualification tests under ECSS-Q-ST-60 / ECSS-E-ST-33 may be performed via established test houses and national facilities. 
NEMA Systems was formed following a decade of close working between NEMA UK Ltd, The University of Nottingham and Ultema Consultancy Ltd. It formalises the trusted relationship and allows NEMA Systems to benefit from the abilities and experience of all three founding parents of the business. Our team has a long history of developing and manufacturing actuators, motors and drives to create electro-mechanical systems for demanding environments. This experience informs the way we approach engineering, verification, manufacturing and programme delivery.
entityDescription:
NEMA Systems Ltd is a UK-based engineering company specialising in advanced electro-mechanical, power electronics, and high-performance drive systems for aerospace, defence, and electrified transport applications.

Formed from a collaborative foundation bringing together expertise across industrial manufacturing, systems engineering, and academic research, NEMA Systems operates at the intersection of innovation and application. The company integrates capabilities spanningelectrical machines, power electronics, control systems, and full system architecture design, enabling the rapid development of high-performance, certifiable technologies for demanding environments.
Our heritage is rooted in a strong UK engineering ecosystem combining:
•Advanced machine design and manufacturing capability.
• Systems engineering and programme delivery expertise.
• World-class academic research in power electronics, machines and control.

This integrated approach allows NEMA Systems to bridge the gap between concept and real-world deployment, supporting customers from early-stage feasibility and modelling through to prototype development, validation, and test

The Power Electronics, Machines and Control Institute at the University of Nottingham (UoN) is a world-leading centre of excellence for cutting-edge electrical aerospace technology.
Following over 30 years in Aerospace actuation primarily in Research and development of electric actuation, Ultema Consultancy Ltd was formed in 2018 by Chris Whitley to provide expertise to existing and emerging actuation companies.

entityDescription:
Darwins Geospatial S.L. is a Spanish Earth-observation company that turns satellite, aerial and drone data into environmental indicators and the software platforms that deliver them. Its work spans two integrated capabilities: the scientific side — deriving and validating indicators of vegetation condition, soil moisture, water stress, soil degradation and habitat conservation status from Copernicus Sentinel and complementary missions, using remote sensing and machine learning — and the engineering side — building the cloud infrastructure, data pipelines and web platforms through which those indicators reach end users, with tenant and user management, large-raster serving and export tooling.Darwin delivers as a technical partner within consortia and directly for institutional clients, covering habitat
mapping and conservation-status assessment, environmental exposure indicators for public-health research, biodiversity and canopy analysis from drone data, and soil erosion modelling. It operates on Google Cloud and object-storage architectures and works with open standards and open-source tooling.

entityDescription:
Precision Resource Slovenia d.o.o., located in Logatec, Slovenia, is part of the global Precision Resource Group and provides advanced precision metal manufacturing solutions for demanding applications.
Our capabilities include metal additive manufacturing, precision CNC machining, fineblanking, tooling, finishing and inspection. Precision Resource combines these technologies to support customers with complex, high-quality metallic components from development and prototyping through industrialized production.
For aerospace and space applications, our focus is on lightweight and geometrically complex components requiring a combination of advanced manufacturing and precision finishing. Metal additive manufacturing capabilities cover titanium, aluminium, nickel-based alloys, stainless steels and other alloys, supported by CNC machining capabilities.
A key capability is the combination of additive manufacturing with precision post-processing, enabling complex near-net-shape components to be followed by machining of critical interfaces, bores, threads, mounting surfaces and other precision features.
We are interested in cooperating with European space companies, system integrators and technology developers seeking a manufacturing partner for satellite structures, mechanisms, payloads, propulsion systems, antenna systems and other precision spaceflight hardware.
Precision Resource's objective is to support customers that retain responsibility for product design, engineering and qualification while requiring a capable industrial partner for component manufacturing, machining, finishing and industrialization.

entityDescription:
Comobi – Orchestrating multimodal, autonomous-ready mobility
Ambition
Comobi BV (Gent, Belgium) runs a mobility platform for shared airport and station transfers. At its core is a proprietary pricing and matching algorithm. It groups passengers into shared rides, sets fair dynamic prices and assigns each trip to the right vehicle. Our ambition goes beyond one vehicle type or one fleet. We want to optimise the mobility system as a whole, planning across cars, vans, buses and, soon, autonomous shuttles as one coordinated network. This means fewer empty kilometres, higher occupancy and a lower cost and carbon footprint per passenger.
Why navigation and satellite technology matter in the shift to autonomy
Today a human driver fills the gaps in any mobility service. They read the traffic, handle a closed road, find the right terminal entrance and adjust when a flight lands early. Autonomous operations remove that human layer, so the intelligence has to move into the system itself.
In an autonomous model, Comobi acts as the service owner. It holds the customer demand, builds the trips and hands assignments to vehicle owners: autonomous operators running their own fleets. For this handover to work reliably, both sides need a shared, precise and constantly updated picture of the operating environment:
- High-integrity positioning and navigation (GNSS, including Galileo's high-accuracy and authentication services), so assignments, pick-up points and handovers are exact and trustworthy
- Satellite-based situational awareness, such as Earth observation, weather and real-time disruption data, so the service layer can re-plan routes, timing and vehicle allocation before problems reach the passenger
- Resilient connectivity, including satellite links where terrestrial networks fall short, so vehicles and the platform stay in contact at all times
Space-based data makes it possible to go from "dispatching a driver" to "orchestrating an autonomous fleet." It gives the service owner the context a human driver used to supply.
Multivendor collaboration
Comobi does not aim to build every component itself. We want to act as the neutral orchestration layer in a multivendor ecosystem. That means working with autonomous vehicle operators, navigation technology providers, satellite data providers and data storage and processing partners, with a preference for local and European partners. Our aim is to launch multivendor pilot operations. In these pilots, assignments, positioning data and situational information flow through open interfaces between the service owner and several vehicle operators. That makes autonomous mobility scalable, interoperable and grounded in European space capabilities.

entityDescription:
InnoTecpLife sp. z o.o. is a special purpose company wholly owned by the Warsaw University of Life Sciences (SGGW). The company was established to support the University in the commercialisation of research results, technology transfer, cooperation with industry, and the development and implementation of research, innovation and business projects.
In its day-to-day activities, InnoTecpLife supports the preparation, management and implementation of R&D projects, including projects financed from national and European funding programmes. The company provides organisational, administrative, financial and contractual support for research and innovation activities, including cooperation between scientific teams and external partners.
InnoTecpLife is also involved in the commercialisation of intellectual property and technologies developed at SGGW, the development and support of university spin-off companies, the establishment of cooperation with business partners, and the preparation and implementation of research and expert services for external entities.
The company also supports the University in identifying funding opportunities, preparing project applications, coordinating project implementation and settlement, organising expert and advisory services, and developing initiatives aimed at transferring scientific knowledge and technologies to the market.
Through these activities, InnoTecpLife acts as an operational bridge between SGGW’s scientific and research potential and the needs of industry, public institutions and other external partners.
